title: Upgrade runbook and failover quota strategy for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Objective: define and implement an operationally safe upgrade runbook and automated failover/quota strategy for dedicated GPU pools to enable LTS channel rollouts with predictable capacity preservation and automated rollback. This ticket consolidates versioning semantics for LTS channels, gate criteria for each rollout phase, autoscaler handoff coordination, and a concise runbook for on-call and SRE during upgrades. The goal is to ensure minimal customer disruption (<= 2% request throttling across dedicated pools) while enabling canary stages and accelerated rollouts for low-risk waves.
acceptance_criteria: A clear mapping from runtime versions -> LTS channels documented in Confluence
A phased gate matrix (smoke -> canary -> ramp -> full) with numeric SLO thresholds and observability queries
Automation hooks for autoscaler handshake that can pause/resume scale-to-zero and drain operations
Runbook steps validated in a dry-run on staging dedicated pools without customer traffic
Rollback action is executable in <10 minutes with documented impact scenarios
runbook: Pre-checks: confirm target LTS mapping and release artifacts; verify model variant compatibility list; ensure GitHub PRs merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8245
Capacity snapshot: capture pool free capacity and in-flight request percentile (p50,p95,p99) via Console dashboard link: https://console.redwood.com/dedicated/pool-capacity
Gate 0 (smoke): deploy to a single control-plane region on a non-critical dedicated pool with 0.5% traffic shadow; verify latency and error delta < 5% for 30 minutes
Gate 1 (canary): schedule progressive node drains on 5% of pool capacity with autoscaler in observe-only mode; validate KV-cache warmup and kernel selection stability; run perf regression tests
Gate 2 (ramp): enable autoscaler handoff policy (autoscaler=live, drain-quota=2x failover-min); gradually increase to 25% pool conversion with 1-hour stabilization windows
Gate 3 (full): release to remaining nodes with staggered waves (max 10% nodes per 15 minutes) and continuous monitoring; final verification for 3 hours

Abort and rollback: if any gate triggers an alert (error rate > 2x baseline OR tail-latency p99 increase > 30% for 10 minutes), immediately pause rollout, shift traffic to fallback variant, and execute rollback script: scripts/rollback_release.sh
Post-upgrade: capture SLO delta report, annotate incident if customer-impacting, update LTS channel docs and finalize release notes
tests: Dry-run on staging: automated waves using the upgrade controller with synthetic traffic generator
Chaos test: simulate NVLink flaps and GPU OOM on a canary node to validate fallback-quota behavior
Autoscaler integration test: verify handshake where orchestrator pauses drains when autoscaler indicates low headroom
KV cache heat test: generate typical prefix distributions to ensure cache warm-up meets >90% hit-rate within 120s
monitoring: Primary KPIs: request success rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, queue length
SLO thresholds: success_rate >= 99.5% across dedicated pools, p99 latency delta <= +20% versus baseline
Dashboards: dedicated-upgrades-ops (Console) and flamegraphs for hot kernels; alert links included
Automated alerts: rollout-halt if error_rate > 2% absolute or sustained p99 > threshold for 10m
Post-mortem anchors: link to incident template and runbook for RCA
